extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners studying peer review, conference organizers, and security/AI researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Creation and analysis of a publicly-released dataset of honest and malicious bidding behavior collected from a mock conference activity, plus evaluation of strategies' effects on reviewer-paper assignment and baseline detection algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public release of dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel dataset is collected and publicly released to fill the gap of no publicly-available data on malicious paper bidding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset should be made publicly available so others can create and evaluate methods to mitigate malicious bidding; dataset provenance and access links should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection via mock conference activity with instructed roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collected from a mock conference activity where participants were instructed to bid either honestly or maliciously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use controlled instructions to elicit both honest and malicious bidding behavior so that labeled examples of different strategies are present for analysis and algorithm evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive analysis of bidding behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a descriptive analysis of the bidding behavior observed in the dataset, including categorization of different strategies employed by participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze patterns in bids, document different malicious strategies, and explain how behaviors differ from honest bidding; use this analysis to inform threat models and detection feature design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of malicious bidding strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize the different strategies malicious reviewers use when bidding (e.g., strategic patterns to influence assignment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and name strategy classes observed in the data; provide examples and characterize the prevalence and signatures of each strategy to support downstream detection efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of strategy effectiveness at manipulating assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the ability of each (malicious) strategy to manipulate the reviewer-paper assignment produced by assignment algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report how much each strategy changes assignment outcomes (e.g., getting a reviewer assigned to a target paper), quantify impact on assignment quality, and compare across strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of detection algorithms and baseline performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the performance of simple algorithms meant to detect malicious bidding, using the collected dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide baseline detection results (metrics, strengths/weaknesses) so future research has a comparison point; discuss which algorithms/features work or fail and under what conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation: bids as inputs to assignment algorithms and threat model
rubrics_metrics.description: Bids are used (along with other data) by paper assignment algorithms to compute high-quality assignments, and malicious reviewers can strategically bid to unethically manipulate that process (e.g., to be assigned to a friend's paper as quid-pro-quo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing datasets, analyses, and defenses, explicitly model the ways bidders can manipulate bids and the downstream effect on assignment algorithms; threat scenarios (such as quid-pro-quo) should be exemplified and considered in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset as enabling resource for mitigation research
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset should enable creation and rigorous evaluation of methods to mitigate malicious bidding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset design and documentation should support experiments to develop and compare mitigation/detection approaches; release should include enough contextual information (instructions, labels, metadata) to make such evaluations reproducible.
